To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the parents of children with childhood cancer experience a significant reduction of work hours and income during the child's active treatment.

parents of children with childhood cancer experience a reduced household income and a more difficult work situation during the treatment period, but the situation is back at the same level as before diagnosis one year after the treatment is finished.
the diagnosis of childhood cancer results in an altered work situation and income for parents in the short- as well as in the long-term.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of childhood cancer on parents, and how parents’ socio-economic conditions are influenced.
the socio-economic conditions for parents of children with a life-threatening disease.
how parents’ work situation, sick-leave and household income are impacted by the diagnosis of their child with cancer, and how these factors change over time.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
parents of children with childhood cancer experience a significant impact on their work situation and household income during their child’s cancer treatment and in the months thereafter.
the parents’ work situation is most evidently impacted during treatment.
the parents of children with childhood cancer in Sweden are at risk for a negative impact on work situation, sick-leave and income in the short and medium term.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the socio-economic impact of childhood cancer on families in Sweden is substantial.

parents of children with a cancer diagnosis experience an altered work situation and household income in the short-term and that these changes are not fully restored in the long-term, and that this is especially true for fathers.

parents of children with acute lymphoblastic leukemia in Sweden have a reduced household income and work situation in the short- to medium-term, and that mothers’ income and work situation are most evidently impacted.
The main takeaway from our work is that
parents of children with childhood cancer need to be supported in their work situation, sick-leave, and income during and after treatment.
the parents’ socio-economic conditions should be monitored during the entire course of the child’s cancer treatment and beyond, in order to provide support and reduce strain for the family.

parents of children with pediatric cancer need to be supported in their role as parents and as workers, and that their work situation and income should be considered in the planning of comprehensive support.
